title: Thai Basil Minced Pork
description: One pork base for our two dinners, with rice or whichever noodles the bubbies fancy.
imageAlt: Reference photograph: Thai basil minced pork beside steamed rice on a simple white oval plate and wooden table.
imageCaption: Reference photograph · Thai basil pork with rice · displayed crop
personalNote: Jack, I’d make the whole kilo of pork so we’ve got dinner for two nights. Save half of the base before adding any noodles, then pick a different carb tomorrow if the bubbies are in a different mood.
equipment: Separate saucepan or bowl for your carb
advancePrep: Peel and chop the onions and garlic, and pick the basil leaves off their stems before heating the wok.
importantNotes: The pork batch makes four portions: two dinners for both of us. The carb quantities are for the two of us for ONE dinner, not both nights. Make the whole pork base once, take half out before mixing in noodles, and use the saved half with a fresh carb on night two. Cooking times are estimates and don’t include soaking noodles.
portionNote: At 4 portions, the pork feeds us for two dinners; the selected carb feeds the two of us tonight.
secondNightNote: For night two, use the half of the pork base we saved in the fridge. Prepare whichever carb we fancy using its steps below, and reheat the saved pork once until it’s steaming hot all the way through. Serve the carb alongside it, or toss cooked noodles through the reheated pork. We can have a fried egg on top if we feel like it.

groups.title: Our pork base for both nights

ingredients.name: 5% lean pork mince
ingredients.note: This is the full batch for our two dinners.

ingredients.name: Onions
ingredients.note: Red or brown, whichever we have; peel and chop.

ingredients.name: Water to loosen the pork
ingredients.note: Only if the base gets too dry.

ingredients.name: Basil leaves
ingredients.note: Pick the leaves off their stems.

groups.title: If we feel like an egg tonight

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.note: Optional: one fried egg for each of us tonight.

steps.title: Get our pork ingredients ready
steps.description: Peel and chop the onions and garlic, and pick the basil leaves off their stems. Have the soy sauces and pepper measured so you’re not looking for things once the mince starts cooking.

steps.title: Brown the mince
steps.description: Get the wok hot on high heat, add the pork mince and squish it around to break up the clumps. Give it about 5 minutes, until it starts browning.

steps.title: Add the onions and garlic
steps.description: Now add the chopped onions and garlic. Let them cook with the pork for 10 minutes while you keep squishing everything around.

steps.title: Add the soy sauces
steps.description: Add the light and dark soy sauces, mix them through and cook for another 5 minutes. We want the base fairly dry, with just a tiny bit of sauce left.
steps.doneness: A fairly dry pork mix with a little sauce.

steps.title: Check how saucy it is
steps.description: If it’s too dry, add the measured water and let it thicken a little. If it’s too saucy, cook it a bit longer so some water dries out. We want enough sauce to coat the pork, rather than a pool at the bottom.
steps.tip: Look at the texture, Jack. Add the water only if we need it.

steps.title: Add the basil and pepper
steps.description: Add the basil leaves and ground black pepper. Squish them through for another minute, then turn the heat off.
steps.warning: Check the mince is fully cooked before serving. A thermometer check is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Save half for our second night
steps.description: Take HALF the pork base out now, before tossing any noodles in. Put it in a shallow container to cool promptly, then refrigerate it for tomorrow. Tonight we’re using the other half of the base.
steps.tip: This is the bit that gives us a second dinner with a different carb.
steps.warning: Cool and put tomorrow’s pork in the fridge within 1–2 hours; use it within 48 hours.

troubleshooting.title: Too dry?
troubleshooting.text: Add the measured water only if we need it, then let it thicken a little.

troubleshooting.title: Too saucy?
troubleshooting.text: Give it a little more time on the heat so the extra water cooks off.

troubleshooting.title: Two nights, two different carbs
troubleshooting.text: Save half the plain pork base before adding noodles. Tomorrow we can choose something different without making another whole batch.

storage: Put tomorrow’s half of the pork in a shallow container so it cools quickly, then refrigerate within 1–2 hours. Eat it within 48 hours. Keep the base separate from the carb so we can make a fresh choice on night two. If we save any cooked rice, cool it ideally within 1 hour and use it within 24 hours.
reheating: Reheat only the saved pork we’re eating, once, until steaming hot all the way through. Serve it with a freshly prepared carb. Any saved rice should be reheated only once, until steaming hot throughout.
foodSafety: The pork mince needs to be fully cooked before we eat it: a thermometer check is 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Cook any optional fried eggs to your liking using British Lion or Laid in Britain hen eggs if the yolks will be runny.
servingSuggestion: Half the pork base for our dinner tonight, half for night two. Choose our carb for tonight, and add a fried egg each if we feel like it.

recipeOptions.label: White rice
recipeOptions.description: Rice tonight? This amount is for the two of us for one dinner.

groups.title: Our carb for tonight (two of us)

ingredients.name: White rice
ingredients.note: Wash three times if possible. This is tonight’s amount for the two of us.

ingredients.name: Water for rice
ingredients.note: For preparing this carb as described below.

beforeSteps.title: Get our rice ready
beforeSteps.description: Wash the white rice in cold water three times if you can. Boil a kettle of water, pour it into our separate rice saucepan and bring it to the boil. You can cook the rice alongside the pork, using its separate timer.

afterSteps.title: Boil and drain the rice
afterSteps.description: Add the washed rice to the boiling water and cook for about 12 minutes, like we do for the kimchi stew. Taste a few grains and check the packet if it needs a different time. Drain it and return it to the rice pot. Keep tonight’s pork warm while this finishes.

afterSteps.title: Rice and pork, and an egg if we fancy it
afterSteps.description: Serve the rice with tonight’s half of the pork base straight away. If we feel like a fried egg on top, fry one for each of us and put it on our plates.
afterSteps.tip: Tomorrow we can choose a different carb with the pork we’ve already saved.

recipeOptions.label: Egg noodles
recipeOptions.description: Egg noodles tonight? Choose 400–500 g for the two of us.
recipeOptions.advancePrep: Have a separate saucepan ready for the noodles.

groups.title: Our carb for tonight (two of us)

ingredients.name: Egg noodles
ingredients.note: Use 400–500 g for the two of us for one dinner.

ingredients.name: Water for egg-noodles
ingredients.note: For preparing this carb as described below.

afterSteps.title: Boil our egg noodles
afterSteps.description: Boil the egg noodles separately, following the packet’s time and instructions. Drain them once they’re cooked.
afterSteps.doneness: Noodles cooked as the packet describes.

afterSteps.title: Noodles beside the pork, or tossed through
afterSteps.description: We can have the cooked egg noodles on the side, or toss them through tonight’s pork. Make sure we’ve already saved half the base for tomorrow before mixing anything in. If we fancy a fried egg on top, fry one for each of us and serve straight away.

recipeOptions.label: Rice vermicelli
recipeOptions.description: Thin rice vermicelli tonight? Choose 400–500 g for the two of us.
recipeOptions.advancePrep: Cold-water soak: 30 minutes. If you forgot, boiling water for 1 minute works too, but makes the noodles a bit softer.

groups.title: Our carb for tonight (two of us)

ingredients.name: Rice vermicelli
ingredients.note: Use 400–500 g for one dinner for the two of us. Soak, then drain.

ingredients.name: Water for rice-vermicelli
ingredients.note: For preparing this carb as described below.

beforeSteps.title: Soak our vermicelli
beforeSteps.description: Soak the rice vermicelli in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain it. If you forgot, use boiling water for 1 minute instead; it makes the noodles a little softer. Get the pork going while the cold-water version soaks.

afterSteps.title: Finish cooking the vermicelli
afterSteps.description: Once the vermicelli has softened, finish cooking it according to its packet until it’s cooked and hot, then drain it. A cold soak softens dried noodles; it isn’t the final cooking step. We can serve the cooked noodles alongside tonight’s pork, or toss them through it.
afterSteps.doneness: Cooked vermicelli, hot through and tender.

afterSteps.title: Serve our vermicelli and pork
afterSteps.description: Check we’ve saved half the pork base before tossing any noodles through tonight’s half. Serve straight away, with a fried egg each if we feel like it.

recipeOptions.label: Flat rice noodles
recipeOptions.description: Flat noodles tonight? Choose 400–500 g for the two of us.
recipeOptions.advancePrep: Like our Char Kway Teow: cold water for 1 hour gives a better texture, or boiling water for 5 minutes if you forgot. The hot-water version will be a bit softer.

groups.title: Our carb for tonight (two of us)

ingredients.name: Flat rice noodles
ingredients.note: Use 400–500 g for one dinner for the two of us. Soak, then drain.

ingredients.name: Water for flat-rice-noodles
ingredients.note: For preparing this carb as described below.

ingredients.name: Hot water to finish flat noodles
ingredients.note: For cooking the soaked noodles in tonight’s pork, using our Char Kway Teow method. Not needed if we boil the noodles separately.

beforeSteps.title: Soak our flat rice noodles
beforeSteps.description: Soak the flat rice noodles in cold water for 1 hour, like our Char Kway Teow, then drain them. If you forgot, soak in boiling water for 5 minutes instead. They’ll be a bit softer, but it doesn’t make a big difference. Get the other ingredients ready while they soak.

afterSteps.title: Cook our flat noodles through
afterSteps.description: If we’re tossing the flat noodles through the pork, check that tomorrow’s half of the base is already out. Add the drained, soaked noodles to tonight’s hot pork, add the hot water measured for finishing them, and toss on high heat for about 5 minutes, like our Char Kway Teow, until they’re cooked but still chewy. If we want noodles on the side instead, finish cooking them following the packet, then drain and serve alongside the pork.
ingredients: Hot water to finish flat noodles
afterSteps.heat: High heat for the wok version
afterSteps.tip: Use the 5-minute timer for cooking the soaked noodles in the wok. For separately boiled noodles, use the packet time.
afterSteps.doneness: Hot, cooked noodles with a little chew.

afterSteps.title: Flat noodles and pork, and an egg if we fancy it
afterSteps.description: Make sure tomorrow’s half of the pork is already out before mixing in any noodles. Serve tonight’s noodles and pork straight away, with a fried egg each if that’s what we fancy.
